_comment: The conformance-hook manifest. NF-5 §4.5 requires that the conformance interface live
outside the production import graph, that the delta between the conformance build and the
production build be ENUMERATED rather than unknown, and that hook routes 404 on the
production digest.
This build declares one hook module: conformance/hook.js. The dependency arrow points one
way — the hook imports the Worker's default export; the Worker imports nothing under
conformance/. That is CH-1, and it is decidable by reading the two import lists rather than
by trusting a comment. hooks.test.js walks the production graph and asserts it.
HONEST ACCOUNTING (NF-5 §4.5). Because a hook module exists, the audited build is NOT
byte-identical to the deployed build, and the digest argument in §8.2 is weakened exactly
as §4.5 says it is. No amount of process removes that. What CH-3 buys is that the delta is
one file, enumerated here, and reviewable in full. An earlier version of this manifest
claimed no hook existed and that the builds were identical; that claim was false, and the
CH-3 assertion that should have caught it computed the conformance file set as
production-union-declared, which is trivially equal to production when nothing is declared.
hooks.test.js now DISCOVERS hook-shaped modules under conformance/ and fails when one is
not declared here, so an undeclared hook is a test failure rather than a silent omission.
Null means 'not pinned in-tree'. Pinning a digest in a source file edited by the same
commit that pins it is a staleness trap, so the digests are computed at audit time by
hooks.test.js and reported. CH-3's reviewable-diff requirement is enforced structurally:
the test asserts the conformance file set minus the production file set is EXACTLY
hook_modules, and that no undeclared hook-shaped module exists. When a release pins these
values, the test verifies them instead of reporting them.
